message.content: {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches on concept and endpoint: each reports trait_reported/trait_efo as abdominal aortic aneurysm and phenotyping_reported is an AAA diagnosis (one is explicitly prevalent AAA). Several models have only full-model discrimination (AUROC/C-index) without PRS-only AUROC, making cross-model performance comparison weak and potentially covariate-driven per the provided domain guidance; others lack AUC/R2 entirely. PGS000753 is preferred as a disease-focused AAA study (Million Veteran Program; Circulation) with explicit endpoint description and a clear PRS effect size (OR per SD 1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) using only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs), avoiding reliance on potentially non-comparable full-model AUROC. Confidence is low because two newer disease-focused PRS-CS models (PGS003972/PGS003973) exist but provide only full-model metrics (0.69 AUROC; 0.882 C-index) with limited PRS-isolated evidence in the context, while the large framework score (PGS001784) provides PRS-only R2 (~0.0147) but comes from a broad cross-trait biobank framework and its high full-model AUROC is not directly comparable."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all indicate abdominal aortic aneurysm or a very close equivalent, including one prevalent endpoint). Among the non-framework, disease-focused options, PGS003972 and PGS003973 come from a dedicated AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet; many contributing cohorts), which domain guidance favors over portability/pan-trait framework scores (PGS001784, PGS002054) and over an older sparse prevalent-endpoint P+T score (PGS000753). Between PGS003972 and PGS003973, the reported discrimination is not cleanly comparable: PGS003972 reports AUROC=0.69 with unknown covariates, while PGS003973 reports C-index=0.882 with only age/age^2/sex (a full-model metric likely dominated by covariates per the provided policy, and not directly comparable to PRS-only metrics). Given this ambiguity, I select PGS003972 because its reported AUROC is closer to a standard classification metric and avoids relying on an unusually high full-model C-index; however, missing PRS-only/incremental metrics and inconsistent metric types across candidates prevent a high-confidence ‘best’ selection."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is prevalent AAA), so selection hinges on comparability of PRS performance and study archetype. Several candidates report only full-model discrimination (e.g., PGS003973 C-index=0.882; PGS001784 AUROC=0.868) or have missing PRS-only AUROC, and domain guidance warns not to substitute full-model AUROC/C-index for PRS-only metrics; this makes the seemingly high discrimination likely covariate-driven and non-comparable. Among models with more PRS-isolated signals, PGS000753 reports an effect size (OR per SD=1.37, 95% CI 1.30–1.44) with basic covariates (age, sex, PCs) and comes from a disease-focused AAA publication context, whereas at least one alternative (PGS002054) is from a portability framework with only a small partial-r reported. However, PGS000753 is sparse (29 variants) and uses a prevalent endpoint, and the newer PRS-CS models from a large AAA meta-analysis family (PGS003972/PGS003973) lack PRS-only metrics and have unknown/variable covariates, so the overall evidence is insufficient to make a clearly strong, conflict-free recommendation—hence low-confidence DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm; one is prevalent). However, comparable PRS-only performance is largely missing/uneven across models: several report only full-model AUROC/C-index (e.g., PGS003973 C-index=0.882 with only age/age^2/sex; PGS001784 full-model AUROC=0.868 but also provides a covariates-regressed-out Nagelkerke R2=0.0147; PGS003429/PGS003972 report full-model AUROC ~0.69–0.71), while others report only partial-r (PGS002054) or only an effect size (PGS000753 OR per SD=1.37). Given domain guidance to avoid substituting full-model AUROC for PRS performance and to prefer disease-focused evidence over pan-trait/framework scores, PGS000753 is selected as a disease-focused AAA study (Circulation; MVP/MAYO-VDB) with a clear per-SD effect size signal, rather than a portability/framework-derived score whose strongest visible advantage is a full-model AUROC. The main limitation is that PGS000753 lacks explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 and competes with multiple newer, endpoint-aligned candidates with larger validation samples and some PRS-comparable R2, making the best-choice evidence insufficiently decisive."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All six candidates are direct matches on trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm), so the decision rests on comparative evidence quality. PGS003972 is preferred because it comes from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis publication context (Nat Genet; many contributing cohorts listed), uses a genome-wide shrinkage method (PRS-CS) consistent with polygenic architecture, and reports a basic full-model discrimination metric (AUROC=0.69) in European evaluation without obviously heavy clinical covariates (covariates are unknown, which is a limitation but not a known leakage pattern). Competing models have notable weaknesses: PGS001784 and PGS002054 come from pan-trait/framework portability-style papers (Global Biobank lessons; UKB portability) with modest PRS-only metrics (e.g., Nagelkerke R2≈0.0147 / partial-r≈0.0144), and PGS000753 is an older, very sparse P+T score (29 variants) with effect size only. PGS003973 reports a very high C-index (0.882), but this is a full-model metric with age/sex covariates and is not directly comparable to PGS-only performance; the large apparent advantage could be covariate-driven per the provided domain policy, and no PRS-only/incremental metric is shown. Overall, the evidence supports PGS003972 as best supported disease-focused choice, but confidence is capped because key PRS-comparable performance metrics (PGS-only AUROC/incremental AUROC) and covariate details are missing or non-comparable across candidates."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). Among them, PGS003972 (PRS-CS; Nat Genet 2023 AAA GWAS meta-analysis) is best supported as a disease-focused, multi-cohort development with a direct AAA endpoint, aligning with the cardiovascular/large-vessel policy preference for newer disease-focused multi-cohort meta-analysis models over older sparse prevalent-endpoint scores. However, the evidence is insufficient for a high-confidence pick because key PRS-comparable metrics are largely missing or not clearly comparable: PGS003972 reports only a full-model AUROC (0.69) with unknown covariates; PGS003973 reports a higher C-index (0.882) but that is likely dominated by age/sex and is not stated as PGS-only; the pan-trait/framework-like scores (PGS001784, PGS002054) provide small PRS-only/partial-r signals (~0.014–0.0147) but come from portability/global-biobank frameworks that domain guidance down-ranks when disease-focused alternatives exist. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Low","rationale":"All six candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and have endpoint-faithful phenotyping_reported (AAA; one explicitly prevalent), so this is not a mismatch problem. {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches by trait_reported/trait_efo and all report an AAA diagnosis-type endpoint in phenotyping_reported (with PGS000753 explicitly prevalent AAA). The strongest disease-focused evidence package is the 2023 Nat Genet AAA GWAS meta-analysis family (PGS003972/PGS003973): large multi-cohort development (many AAA-relevant cohorts listed) with PRS-CS genome-wide construction and European evaluation. Between the two near-clones, PGS003973 shows a higher reported full-model C-index (0.882) but with limited clarity on comparability (C-index vs AUROC; full-model metric; only basic covariates listed), while PGS003972 reports a lower AUROC (0.69) but has more validation records (record_count=3) suggesting more supporting evaluations in-catalog. Given domain guidance not to let a single full-model metric dominate and to prefer coherent disease-focused families over framework scores, I select PGS003972 as the best-supported within the strongest study family, but confidence is tempered because neither model provides explicit PRS-only AUROC/R2 and covariates are unknown for PGS003972, making cross-model performance comparability unresolved."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS000753","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported are abdominal aortic aneurysm or prevalent AAA). {"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS003972","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches (trait_reported/trait_efo and phenotyping_reported all correspond to abdominal aortic aneurysm or a near-equivalent AAA diagnosis endpoint). Two candidates (PGS003972, PGS003973) come from a disease-focused AAA GWAS meta-analysis (Nat Genet, 2023), which domain guidance prefers over pan-trait/portability framework scores when endpoint alignment is comparable. Between those two, PGS003972 has a more coherent PRS-relevant evidence package in the visible metadata: it reports a modest full-model AUROC (0.69) without obviously heavy covariates (covariates listed as Unknown) and is supported by multiple validation records (record_count=3), whereas PGS003973’s very high C-index (0.882) is difficult to interpret as PRS contribution because it is a full model with age/age^2/sex and lacks any PGS-only or covariate-regressed-out metric; thus its apparent superiority may be largely covariate-driven per the provided domain rules. Confidence is only Moderate (and outcome sub-optimal) because most candidates lack PRS-only AUROC/incremental metrics, covariates are unknown for PGS003972, and the strongest PRS-only metric in the set (PGS001784 Nagelkerke R2 covariates-regressed-out=0.0147 in a very large EUR evaluation) comes from a framework-style global biobank paper, creating residual competition that cannot be resolved cleanly from the available fields."}

{"outcome":"DIRECT_SUB_OPTIMAL","best_model_id":"PGS004606","confidence":"Moderate","rationale":"All 6 candidates are direct matches at the trait_efo level (age-related macular degeneration), but they differ materially in endpoint fidelity and interpretability of reported performance. PGS004606 is preferred because it has a clear, directly aligned disease endpoint (phenotyping_reported: age-related macular degeneration), comes from a disease-focused AMD genetics study (Nat Genet; IAMDGC training/development cohort), and reports discrimination (full_model AUROC=0.71) and an effect size (OR per SD=1.76, 95% CI 1.73–1.78) with only basic covariates (age, sex, PCs 1–10), plus a large validation sample size (n=163,011, European). Key limitation: the available AUC appears to be a full-model metric (not explicitly PGS-only or incremental), so cross-model comparability is imperfect; additionally, PGS004952 reports a higher AUROC but on a narrower endpoint (late AMD) and with a very small validation sample (n=1,232) and a likely reporting inconsistency (AUROC listed as 84.2 in classification_metrics), making it less reliable as a clear winner. The UK Biobank portability-framework scores (PGS001834/PGS002041) provide only modest partial correlations (~0.016–0.018) and are from a pan-trait portability context, and PGS002269’s phenotyping_reported is a retinal layer thickness proxy rather than direct AMD diagnosis, so they are less endpoint-faithful for generic AMD risk."}
